candidates.title: Nondegeneracy of the bubble for a fourth-order Liouville boundary problem
candidates.abstract: We establish the nondegeneracy of the bubble for \[ Δ^2u=0\quad \text{in }\mathbb R^4_+,\qquad \partial_tu=0,\quad \partial_tΔu=e^{24π^2u} \quad \text{on }\partial\mathbb R^4_+. \] Using Fourier analysis, stereographic projection and a removable-singularity argument, we classify the weighted $L^2$ boundary kernel without assuming boundedness of the boundary solution. This determines the bounded half-space kernel. Both kernels are generated by dilation and tangential translations. We further obtain sharp estimates for the projected spherical inverse.

candidates.title: Short quadratic exponential sums with primes in major arcs
candidates.abstract: Using the second moment of Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line over the major arcs ${\mathfrak M}({\mathscr L}^b)$, with $τ=y^3x^{-1}{\mathscr L}^{-b_1}$, and excluding a small neighborhood of the centers of these arcs, i.e., those $α$ satisfying $|α-\frac{a}{q}|>(8πy^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{1-\frac{\scriptstyle1}{\scriptstyle{9-4\sqrt{2}}}}{\mathscr L}^{c_2}$, where $c_2=\frac{2A+24+(\sqrt{2}-1)b_1}{2\sqrt{2}-1}$, we obtain the estimate $$ S_2(α;x,y)=\sum_{x-y<n\le x}Λ(n)e(αn^2)\ll y\,{\mathscr L}^{-A}. $$ Moreover, in a small neighborhood of the center of the major arcs, defined by $|α-\frac{a}{q}|\le(8πy^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{\frac{\scriptstyle5}{\scriptstyle8}}{\mathscr L}^{1,5A+0,25b+18}$, an asymptotic formula with a remainder term is obtained for $S_2(α;x,y)$, where $A$, $b_1$, and $b$ are arbitrary fixed positive constants, and ${\mathscr L}=\ln xq$.

candidates.title: A Realizability-Based Kinetic-Fluid Domain Decomposition Method for Single-Temperature Gas Mixtures
candidates.abstract: This paper introduces a domain-adaptive numerical method for multi-species kinetic models that relax toward a single-temperature and single-velocity hydrodynamic limit. To this end, we derive moment realizability matrices for this regime. In this way the ideas of Levermore, Morokoff, and Nadiga are extended to non-equilibrium mixtures in which inter-species and intra-species collisions occur at comparable rates, so that all species relax to a common velocity and a common temperature. The realizability conditions are used as an indicator to divide the computational domain, at each time step, into macroscopic and kinetic regions. In the kinetic regions, where the continuum description fails (e.g., across strong shocks, non-equilibrium interfaces, or kinetic boundary layers), the method solves the multi-species kinetic equations. Close to local thermodynamic equilibrium, the Euler equations of the mixture are solved instead. Confining the kinetic computations to the non-equilibrium regions reduces the simulation time, while the results remain close to those of the full kinetic solver. The method is discretized on Cartesian grids with high-order schemes in space and time. The kinetic e

candidates.title: Near-Quadratic Sample Compression for All VC Classes
candidates.abstract: The sample compression conjecture is a longstanding open problem in learning theory, originating in the work of Littlestone and Warmuth in the 1980s. At its heart is a connection between simplification and generalization: if a predictor consistent with a training sample is defined using only a small part of that sample, then it is likely to generalize. Sample compression schemes formalize this idea, and many natural learning algorithms can be analyzed this way. The sample compression conjecture of Floyd and Warmuth (1995) asserts that every binary concept class of VC dimension $d$ admits a sample compression scheme of size $O(d)$; a weaker conjecture asks only for size polynomial in $d$. Both have remained open: the first bound depending only on $d$, due to Moran and Yehudayoff (2016), is exponential in $d$. We prove the weaker conjecture by constructing a sample compression scheme of size $O(d^2 \log^2 d)$.

candidates.title: Infinity-Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Principal Component Analysis: Exact Reformulation, Finite-Sample Guarantee, and Efficient Algorithm
candidates.abstract: Principal component analysis (PCA) is a fundamental and ubiquitous technique for dimension reduction and representation learning, yet its empirical formulation remains vulnerable to distributional uncertainty. While distributionally robust optimization (DRO) offers a natural remedy, existing order-2 Wasserstein models of PCA either preserve the nominal PCA subspace or lack an exact reformulation. This paper demonstrates how the infinity-Wasserstein distance can reconcile these two desirable properties. For the resulting DRO model of PCA, we derive an exact finite-dimensional reformulation and explicitly identify a worst-case distribution attaining the inner maximum. Crucially, the reformulated objective retains samplewise residual information beyond the empirical covariance matrix, revealing a mechanism through which distributional robustness can reshape the learned principal subspace. Under the mild assumption that the true distribution has a finite fourth moment, we further establish a uniform finite-sample performance guarantee for the proposed model. An iteratively reweighted majorization-minimization algorithm is also developed to solve the resulting nonconvex and nonsmooth op

candidates.title: Quantum Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport in spacetime through spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac distributions and spatiotemporal states
candidates.abstract: Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport is a mathematical framework that determines the most efficient way to transform one probability distribution into another while minimizing a given cost function. Its central constructions include the Wasserstein distances, which quantify the space of probability distributions, and dual formulations that link to convex analysis. Its standard quantum generalization replaces probability distributions with density operators and cost function with positive semidefinite cost operator, which should be regarded as spatial quantum optimal transport. In this work, we propose the quantum optimal transport problem in spacetime through the spatiotemporal phase-space Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distribution and spatiotemporal states and through spatiotemporal state. We show that the two formalisms are equivalent and related via spatiotemporal operator frames. In the Kirkwood-Dirac phase-space formalism, the spatiotemporal distribution and the cost function are complex-valued, and the spatiotemporal couplings are Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distributions that yield the correct marginals for the local states. In the spatiotemporal state formalism, the co

candidates.title: Finite regularity moduli stacks through diffeology
candidates.abstract: Diffeological non-Abelian Hodge theory motivates the study of $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and flat bundles for finite $r$. In this article, we provide a uniform language for treating moduli stacks parametrizing such objects in terms of diffeology. More specifically, we develop a theory of stacks presentable by diffeological groupoids over the site of $C^r$ manifolds for arbitrary $r$. As an application, we construct moduli stacks over the sites of $C^r$ manifolds parametrizing $C^r$ vector bundles over a smooth manifold, and $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and of flat bundles over a complex manifold. We also construct $C^r$ versions of the non-Abelian Hodge filtration stack, interpolating between Higgs bundles and flat bundles through $λ$--connections. We show that all these stacks are presentable by diffeological groupoids. Finally, we construct moduli stacks parametrizing $C^r$ families of $Δ^n$--shaped diagrams of these objects, and show that they assemble into simplicial stacks whose levels are all presentable by diffeological groupoids.

candidates.title: Symmetry classification of hyperfine rovibrational molecular phase space
candidates.abstract: Symmetry-based structures have advanced molecular spectroscopy and quantum information science, yet connections between these fields remain largely unexplored. We construct a phase space theory of a molecule by jointly treating rotational, vibrational, and nuclear-spin degrees of freedom as the quotient of orientations and normal coordinates by the molecule's point group. The various combinations of how these three degrees of freedom transform under symmetries organize a molecule's states into molecular species, and we show that each species is defined by a particular absolutely maximally entangled (AME) carrier state, or, for 45 species, by a two-dimensional space of them. Up to local unitaries and the order of the sectors, molecular species realize 21 AME states across 75 point groups: a product state, four maximally entangled pairs, and 16 genuinely tripartite states. A Fourier transform on the quotient relates orientation and angular-momentum descriptions while preserving these carrier states. We propose an example experimental protocol for preparing and driving symmetry-adapted bend states of $\mathrm{CaOCH_3}$.

candidates.title: The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
candidates.abstract: We prove that three is the smallest background period for which a one-dimensional discrete Anderson-Bernoulli operator can have infinitely many gaps in its almost-sure spectrum. For an explicit period-three background and coupling, we construct infinitely many bounded gaps accumulating from the right at a spectral energy, for every nondegenerate Bernoulli law. This property persists on an open set of background and coupling parameters. The proof combines a transverse heteroclinic connection and invariant multicones with spectral points from periodic realizations. A strict geometric window permits integer scale matching, and the required parameter inequalities are verified by exact rational arithmetic.

candidates.title: Quantum Born Geometries from Modular Quantization
candidates.comment: 15 pages, to be submitted to PoS Proceedings of the Corfu Summer Institute 2026 "Workshop on Noncommutative and Generalised Geometries and their Physical Applications" (CORFU2026) 13 September - 21 September 2026, Corfu, Greece
candidates.abstract: A structural link between quantization and "thermal-doubled" non-commutative Born geometry (with its split-quaternionic structure) is uncovered via Tomita-Takesaki first-quantized modular theory for complexified and polarized ortho-symplectic spaces. Implications for the modular algebraic quantum gravity program (arXiv:1007.4094) hint at further deep modifications of the notions of space and geometry (thermal quantum space-time hypothesis) waiting to be further explored. Speculative suggestions in the direction of A.Sakharov and L.Boyle-K.Finn-N.Turok CPT-mirror cosmologies will be mentioned, among several others. The present work is based on the manuscript "Modular Quantization and Non-commutative Space-time" (now on alphaXiv) that has been shared, with a selected number of researchers, since end of April 2026.

candidates.title: Hyperlyve: Parallelized Enumeration and Exact Lyapunov Stability Certification for Deep ReLU Networks
candidates.abstract: We introduce Hyperlyve (Hyperplane Partitioned Lyapunov Verification and Enumeration), a framework for proving the asymptotic stability of nonlinear dynamical systems, including those with neural network controllers. Hyperlyve learns and formally certifies continuous piecewise-affine (CPA) neural Lyapunov functions within a counterexample-guided inductive synthesis (CEGIS) loop. Hyperlyve's key innovation is a parallel algorithm that enumerates the hyperplane arrangement formed by the ReLU activations of deep networks and certifies that Lyapunov conditions hold within each polyhedral region. We derive sound and complete regional tests to verify the asymptotic stability of the exact smooth dynamics (rather than a piecewise-linear approximation) within a compact domain of interest. Furthermore, we formally characterize the computational complexity of the CPA neural Lyapunov verification problem as co-NP-complete, filling a key gap in the literature. Empirical results demonstrate that Hyperlyve enumerates ReLU networks over 150-times faster than competing tools, which contributes to Hyperlyve proving the asymptotic stability of systems that are currently intractable for state-of-the-a

candidates.title: In-Context Estimation and Prediction for Parametric ODEs
candidates.abstract: Transformers have demonstrated the ability to perform in-context learning, that is, to adapt to new tasks from a few examples without updating their parameters. Existing theory has largely focused on emulating gradient-based algorithms for convex statistical problems or establishing general function approximation guarantees without exploiting the underlying statistical structure. We study in-context parameter estimation and trajectory prediction for parametric ordinary differential equations (ODEs), where estimation is generally nonconvex. Under suitable identifiability and regularity conditions, we construct a transformer that estimates unknown system parameters from noisy trajectory observations through a two-stage approximate maximum likelihood procedure: a coarse search provides an initialization within a locally strongly convex region, followed by gradient descent with local linear contraction. For prediction, we compose this estimator with a neural approximation of the ODE solution map. We further show that, through parameter sharing, a single transformer can perform both parameter estimation and trajectory prediction simultaneously. For these constructions, we establish nona

candidates.title: Correspondence-Free Camera Pose Estimation by Matching Moments
candidates.comment: 65 pages, including references and appendices; under review
candidates.abstract: The blind perspective-$n$-point (PnP) problem is to estimate the pose of a calibrated camera from 2D and 3D point sets with unknown correspondences. We show that, for complete, noiseless observations, fourteen permutation-invariant image moments up to order four identify a fixed camera pose for almost every 3D point set containing at least twenty points. Our learning-free method, MomentPnP, matches these moments between the observed 2D points and the projected 3D points to initialize a camera pose without correspondences and refines the pose and correspondence weights using expectation--maximization. Across the test sets of three benchmarks, our method reduces median rotation error by $5$--$170\times$ relative to the best learned baseline, both with and without outliers. We recover accurate poses even with as many outliers as inliers. On dense ETH3D scans, pose accuracy improves as the point sets grow, even as individual correspondences become harder to resolve.

candidates.title: A Differential Theory of Quality-Resource Trade-offs for AI Model Selection: The Multiresource Frontier and Its Minimax Price
candidates.abstract: Comparing AI models across resource budgets yields quality-resource frontiers relating error to latency, parameter count, training compute, and energy. Offset power laws summarize such frontiers, but their fitted parameters reveal neither the price-independent geometry nor the manner in which trade-offs extend across several resource channels. This paper addresses both gaps by developing a differential theory in which this structure is made explicit. Each frontier admits a price-independent plane-curve representation relating the effective number of active resource channels, $N_{\mathrm{eff}} = s^2/κ$ (squared slope over curvature), to the remaining log-error depth, $ΔS = \ln(\varepsilon/\varepsilon_{\infty})$. This representation separates intrinsic shape from the scale and origin of the resource axis. Complete monotonicity and divisibility yield differential inequalities and frontier bounds. When each of $N$ resources contributes one active channel, the theory gives the parameter-free operating rule $N_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1$ in delivered units and derives minimax resource prices $λ^{\star}_i = α_i/(N+1)$ with an exact worst-case regret of $\ln(N+1)$ nats. candidates.title: Physics-Spawned Neural Integration of Rotating Shallow-Water Dynamics
candidates.abstract: Equation-derived neural integration can execute prescribed dynamics without training, while informative ensemble learning can estimate uncertain parameters and identify governing interactions without requiring differentiability. Together, these approaches motivate Physics-Spawned Informative Networks ($Φ$SpIN), a framework for prescribed and adaptive hybrid dynamical systems. As a first step toward flood modeling applications, we present $Φ$SpIN-SW, its prescribed-physics realization for the rotating shallow-water equations. Compatible C-grid operators on spherical Voronoi meshes define a computational graph that retains non-polynomial operations and advances the state through recurrent neural integration compiled with JAX. Analytical benchmarks characterize numerical errors, and global and coastal experiments closely reproduce reference solutions generated using the Model Prediction Across Scales (MPAS) model. At approximately 14~km global resolution, A100, H200 and B200 GPUs attain 9-, 19- and 34-fold higher timestep throughput than a 96-core MPAS-SW CPU reference under matched workloads. candidates.title: State-space symmetry in Boolean network ensembles
candidates.abstract: Studies of evolving Boolean network systems have found that Boolean functions cluster into equivalence classes with a characteristic frequency distribution - a pattern governed by the Zyklenzeiger symmetry group - but the dynamical origin of this symmetry has remained unexplained. Here we show that it is a consequence of a fundamental symmetry of Boolean network dynamics itself. A Boolean network consists of nodes that update according to Boolean functions of their regulatory inputs; its global dynamics is encoded in a state-space network. We identify the dynamical symmetry group of ensembles of Boolean networks that average over random interaction topologies: for networks with $N$ nodes, it is the $N$-dimensional hyperoctahedral group, generated by node-flips and node-label permutations. These transformations are admissible for every Boolean network regardless of topology; for random-topology ensembles, including all ensembles of fixed in-degree $K<N$, they constitute the complete symmetry group. candidates.title: Bellman Residual Bracketing: Resolving the Sample Complexity of Discounted and Average-Reward RL
candidates.abstract: We study the sample complexity of the empirical planning or plug-in approach for reinforcement learning (RL) with a generative model. We show the discounted plug-in approach finds an $\varepsilon$-optimal policy with $O(SA (1-γ)^{-3} \varepsilon^{-2} \log(SA/δ))$ samples, where $S, A, γ, δ$ are the state and action sizes, discount factor, and failure probability, respectively. In the average-reward setting, we show that discounted plug-in and direct (undiscounted) plug-in achieve $O(SAH\varepsilon^{-2}\log(SA/δ))$ and $O(SAD\varepsilon^{-2}\log(SA/δ))$ complexities, respectively, where $H$ upper-bounds the optimal bias span and $D$ is the diameter. Combining with our lower bounds for nonadaptive generative models, these results resolve the minimax sample complexity of discounted RL and average-reward RL --- in both the span- and diameter-based classes --- up to constant factors. Our main technical contribution is a novel Bellman residual bracketing technique which improves the efficiency of prior absorbing-MDP-based concentration analyses.

candidates.title: Sharp condition for the existence of wave operators
candidates.abstract: We study the wave operators for a Jacobi matrix whose spectral measure satisfies the Szegő condition. We formulate a sufficient condition in terms of the associated Verblunsky parameters and show that it is sharp.

candidates.title: Mean-field Token Steering
candidates.abstract: We consider stochastic token steering through a deep stack of transformer layers as a mean-field control problem for an interacting particle system on the unit sphere, where interactions arise from the attention mechanism. In the mean-field limit, the token population evolves via a controlled integro-partial differential equation where the feedback control acts as a corrective vector field guiding the population toward an aggregate configuration of tokens in the representation space. We deduce the minimum effort control to accomplish this task over a fixed time horizon interpreted as normalized layer depth. We show that the resulting controlled dynamics for the token population can be understood as a mean-field Schrödinger bridge adapted to the sphere geometry. Building on this, we propose a novel generalization of the dynamic Sinkhorn recursion to compute the consistent token evolution. Numerical experiments confirm that the proposed approach achieves exact steering of the token population.

candidates.title: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
candidates.abstract: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories. Finally, we conjecture, using the Lazard correspondence, a relation between expectation values of line operators in the two types of theories, and test it in examples.

candidates.title: The Triangular Abrikosov Constant and the Thomas--Fermi $Γ$-Limit of Rotating Bose--Einstein Condensates
candidates.abstract: We resolve the Abrikosov coefficient conjecture for rapidly rotating two-dimensional Bose--Einstein condensates within the variational framework of $Γ$-convergence. For a harmonic trap, we establish the $Γ$-convergence of the rescaled Gross--Pitaevskii energy functionals in the fast-rotation regime, through weak $L^2$ convergence of the rescaled densities, and identify the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with $b_\triangle$, the Abrikosov ratio associated with the triangular vortex lattice. The limiting Thomas--Fermi functional determines the first correction to the minimum energy and the macroscopic density of almost minimizers. For the auxiliary rescaled model and its lowest-Landau-level restriction, we also compute a strictly positive limiting $L^2$ distance between minimizing densities and the Thomas--Fermi profile. The identification of the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with the triangular Abrikosov ratio $b_\triangle$ relies on the sharp Gaussian-minorant theorem established in a recent OpenAI preprint~\cite[Theorem~1.2]{Atomic}. candidates.title: A time-domain adversarial example demonstrating the failure of $H^1$ elements in $a$-$φ$ electromagnetic simulation
candidates.abstract: Frequently, $H^1$ continuous finite elements are used in computational electromagnetics despite it being widely known that such an interpolation is not guaranteed to furnish reliable approximations of solutions to general initial/boundary value problems. It is mathematically more natural to use $H(\text{Curl})$ elements (edge elements) than $H^1$ elements, since the former form part of a discrete complex that respects the differential-geometric structure of Maxwell's equations while the latter do not. However, most work discussing the failure of $H^1$ elements for electromagnetics is esoteric and concrete examples demonstrating the clear advantage of edge elements are generally restricted to quasi-static, frequency-domain, or eigenvalue problems. In this work, we summarize essential facts regarding $H^1$ and $H(\text{Curl})$ elements and present a physically feasible yet intentionally adversarial time-domain eddy-current example demonstrating the failure of gauge-penalized $H^1$ elements in an $a$-$φ$ formulation compared to gauge-free mixed scalar/edge $H^1/H(\text{Curl})$ elements. candidates.title: Spectral isometries and invertibility preservers on Banach algebras
candidates.abstract: We prove that every unital surjective complex-linear spectral isometry between complex unital semisimple Banach algebras is a Jordan isomorphism, thereby giving an affirmative answer to the spectrum-preserving form of Kaplansky's conjecture. We also characterize surjective complex-linear maps between arbitrary unital Banach algebras that preserve invertibility in either direction, satisfy either spectral inclusion, or preserve the spectral radius. In particular, for a complex-linear bijection between semisimple Banach algebras, preservation of invertibility in either direction implies preservation in both directions, and either spectral inclusion implies equality of spectra, even without assuming unitality. As an application, we study preservers of the Fredholm essential spectrum and essential spectral radius.

candidates.title: Control of Complex Social Systems via Committed Minorities and Opinion Broadcast
candidates.abstract: Complex social systems are often characterized by a deep interconnection between individuals' opinion formation and their decision-making processes. In this chapter, we show how these two dynamics can be incorporated within a unifying game-theoretic coevolutionary model for actions and opinions. We present the main theoretical results concerning the convergence of the coevolutionary model, and its recent extensions to incorporate further features of real-world social systems. Then, we focus on the problem of controlling such a coevolutionary model. In particular, we present two distinct approaches: i) introducing a committed minority in the population, and ii) broadcasting information to some target individuals. For both of these methods, we discuss their implementation and provide theoretical guarantees on their performance. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control methods on different case studies, illustrating their implementation on simple academic examples, as well as exploring their performance in realistic scenarios using network structures inferred from real-world data. candidates.title: Differentially Private Score Estimation with Applications to Score-Based Generative Models
candidates.abstract: Estimating the score function of a distribution plays a central role in statistics and machine learning, with applications in distribution estimation, sampling, and score-based generative modeling. However, learning scores from sensitive data raises privacy concerns. These concerns are particularly pronounced in score-based generative modeling, where trained models may memorize individual training examples and expose sensitive information through membership inference and data extraction attacks. Although non-private score estimation has been extensively studied, the statistical limits of its private counterpart remain less understood. In this work, we study score estimation under $(α,β)$-differential privacy for $d$-dimensional sub-Gaussian distributions with locally $γ$-Hölder-continuous scores. We develop a sampling-based private score estimator using quadratic B-splines and the exponential mechanism, and we implement our proposal through projected Langevin Monte Carlo with runtime polynomial in the sample size $n$. candidates.title: Faithful Generative Modeling for Censored Time-to-Event Data: From Distributional Fidelity to Statistical Inference
candidates.abstract: Synthetic data has emerged as a powerful tool for data sharing, clinical trial simulation, and digital twin development, with growing applications in biomedical research and drug development. However, limited attention has been devoted to synthetic time-to-event data, which are central to clinical trials and survival analysis. In particular, theoretical guarantees for the distributional fidelity of synthetic survival data remain largely unexplored. More importantly, even when a generator achieves distributional fidelity, it remains unclear whether the downstream statistical analysis is reliable. To address these gaps, we propose a general two-stage generative framework for survival data (TSGSurv) that jointly generates observed times and covariates conditional on event status, and establish its distributional convergence rate. Focusing on the widely used Cox proportional hazards model, we establish conditions under which generator fidelity guarantees consistency of model coefficient estimates. candidates.title: A Hopf algebra action on the cohomology of moduli of abelian varieties
candidates.abstract: We show that the rational compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal{A} = \bigsqcup_{g \geq 0} \mathcal{A}_g$ of principally polarized abelian varieties is free as a bigraded module over the Hopf algebra formed by its weight-zero subspace. The action arises from a symplectic analog of the Waldhausen $S$-construction. This structure yields new lower bounds for Betti numbers and the dimensions of the graded pieces of the weight filtration on the cohomology of $\mathcal{A}_g$. In particular, $\dim H_c^{2g + k}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ grows at least exponentially with $g$ for every nonnegative $k \neq 1, 3$. We also give conjectural descriptions of the full mixed Hodge structures in genera four and five, and of mixed Tate subquotients of $H_c^{2g}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ associated with shuffle algebras and multiple zeta values in every genus.

candidates.title: Convexity is overrated: Shortest paths on 4-polytopes are hard to compute
candidates.abstract: We prove that computing geodesic distance on the boundary of a rational convex $4$-polytope is NP-hard. We then construct rational $4$-polytopes with two rational points joined by exponentially many shortest paths of equal rational length, disproving several conjectures along the way. For the same problem, we also prove SQRTSUM-hardness under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions. By a separate argument, we show that the square of the geodesic distance between distinct rational boundary points of a rational convex polytope is a totally positive multiquadratic number.

candidates.title: The Clifford Hierarchy from Clifford Stabilizers in 2D
candidates.abstract: The Bravyi-König theorem limits the constant-depth logical gates of 2D topological Pauli stabilizer codes to be in the Clifford group. Known qubit codes with Clifford stabilizers exceed it by only one level of the Clifford hierarchy, and this was conjectured to hold generally. We show that this bound can be completely bypassed, and that topological codes with Clifford stabilizers in 2D can realize transversal logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy. We present two explicit constructions of codes based on copies of the quantum doubles of $D_4$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2$, with $k$ logical qubits and a logical $C^{k-1}Z$ gate, which is at level $k$ of the Clifford hierarchy. The physical circuits realizing the gates consist only of physical $Z$ or $CZ$ gates. The main new ingredient comes from the logical encoding, which depends crucially on non-Abelian group multiplication.

candidates.title: Learning the Anyon Atlas
candidates.abstract: We extend our previous search for the modular data of topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions from 22 to 42 anyons, identifying 150,679 new modular data. We do so by adding to our algorithm three rejection gates, two of them based on logistic regression, that discard representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ unlikely to yield modular data. We estimate that roughly 80% of the modular data between ranks 23 and 42 has been identified after closing under known constructions. With this data, we find counterexamples to a conjecture of Geiko and Moore that the reality of the higher Gauss sums suffices for time-reversal symmetry in Chern-Simons theories, and propose a refined criterion. We demonstrate the scalability of this gated implementation by identifying prime modular data at rank 100 that is not realized by any Chern-Simons theory. The identified data through rank 42 has been made available at https://AnyonAtlas.org, to which further data will be added as it is found.

candidates.title: An Atiyah--Hirzebruch to Adams map and the hastened Adams spectral sequence for supercohomology
candidates.abstract: We construct a map of filtered spectra inducing a map from the Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral sequence (AHSS) to the Baker--Lazarev Adams spectral sequence of a $\mathit{ko}$-module $M$. Using this and a theorem of Bruner--Rognes, we construct a hastened Adams spectral sequence (HASS) for the Postnikov truncations of $\mathit{ko}$ and the connective Adams summand. Then, motivated by questions in quantum field theory, topological phases of matter, and tensor category theory, we apply the HASS to supercohomology, the cohomology theory $I_{\mathbb{C}^\times}(τ_{\le 2}\mathit{ko})$, and observe that in examples of interest it is easier to calculate with than either the AHSS or the usual Adams spectral sequence. We include a User's Guide to the HASS and several worked examples, as well as hastened Adams charts for many commonly encountered $\mathcal{A}(1)$-modules.

candidates.title: Diffusion Models are Provably Efficient Priors for Sparse Recovery
candidates.abstract: Diffusion models have transformed generative modeling through their ability to capture and generate samples from complex data distributions. This success has spurred substantial interest in using pretrained diffusion models as expressive priors for highly ill-posed inverse problems in imaging and sensing. Despite strong empirical performance, theoretical understanding of this approach remains limited: existing guarantees are often asymptotic or entail prohibitive computational costs in the worst case. In this paper, we address this gap by studying sparse recovery from a small number of linear measurements, a classical problem in compressed sensing. We show that, given an accurate diffusion model capturing a sparsity-promoting Bernoulli-Gaussian prior, a likelihood-guided annealed Langevin sampler provably recovers the sparse signal in polynomial time with near-optimal sample complexity for a broad family of random and deterministic sensing matrices. When the signal is indeed drawn from the postulated prior, we further establish total variation guarantees for posterior sampling after a final denoising step. These results lay a theoretical foundation for statistically and computation

candidates.title: Boundaries of groups with compact-by-amenable decomposition
candidates.abstract: We look at the Liouville property (triviality of harmonic functions) of topological groups G relative to a compact subgroup K. We show that Gelfand pairs have this property. Furthermore, we show that this property holds if and only if G admits a product decomposition G = K S for an amenable subgroup S. We identify the Poisson and Furstenberg boundaries of these groups. This applies in particular to reductive algebraic groups over local fields.

candidates.title: Rare-Tail Statistics For Learning Biased Gaussian Halfspaces with Label Noise
candidates.abstract: We revisit the classical problem of learning general Gaussian halfspaces in the presence of label noise, with particular focus on the large-bias regime, where information-computation gaps are conjectured in several standard label-noise models. Concretely, we present and analyze the rare-tail mean estimator, an extremely simple one-shot statistic that averages only the observed minority class. In the large-bias regime, classical Averaging (Servedio, 1999) and related global first-moment statistics are provably suboptimal, while the rare-tail mean estimator recovers the target halfspace direction at the information-theoretic sample rate (modulo log factors) under a broad class of label noise models, including probit noise and margin-dependent noise with very slow decay away from the boundary. Notably, our guarantees allow labels arbitrarily close to the decision boundary to be nearly random, while still giving strong directional recovery from a small number of samples. candidates.title: AG-BFGS: Foundations for Accelerated Geometry Learning
candidates.abstract: We introduce an accelerated geometry-learning framework for BFGS that incorporates momentum into the learning of Hessian inverse approximations. We prove that the resulting accelerated updates satisfy explicit stability conditions and preserve positive definiteness within admissible parameter regions. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent improvements over the corresponding non-accelerated schemes while maintaining numerical stability. These results provide the first rigorous theoretical foundation for accelerated quasi-Newton learning and bridge the gap between empirical observations and mathematical guarantees for accelerated second-order methods.

candidates.title: Free energy distribution for two non-crossing directed polymers on the cylinder
candidates.abstract: We consider the partition sum $Z_L(t)$ of two non-crossing continuum directed polymers of length $t$, in a common random medium with the geometry of a cylinder of circumference length $L$. In the limit $t \to +\infty$, the $k$-th cumulant of (minus) the free energy $\log Z_L(t)$, grows as $c_k(L) t$, and we compute the amplitudes $c_k(L)$. To this aim we first study the integer moments $\langle Z_L(t)^n \rangle$, whose long-time behavior is determined by the ground-state energy of the one-dimensional attractive Lieb--Liniger model in the symmetry sector associated with the Young diagram $(n,n)$ (a two-component bosonic nested Bethe ansatz). This ground state energy is obtained using the nested Bethe-Ansatz involving $2n$ physical rapidities and $n$ auxiliary rapidities. The analytic continuation in the replica number $n$, which yields the cumulants $c_k(L)$, is performed through a non-trivial generalization of the method developed by Brunet and Derrida for a single polymer on the cylinder. We obtain fully explicit formulas for the mean $c_1(L)$ and the variance $c_2(L)$, and construct a systematic scheme for computing all higher cumulants $c_k(L)$. Finally, taking $L\to+\infty$ and

candidates.abstract: In a recent paper [J. Phys. A: Math. Theor. 59 175201 (2026)] Green's triple relations for parafermions and parabosons were extended by including a new operator $P$, referred to as the parity operator. The spectrum of $P$ in Fock space representations was computed, making use of the action of parafermion (resp.\ paraboson) creation and annihilation operators. In the current paper, we adopt a different method to compute the spectrum of $P$, namely using character formulas. For a set of $n$ parafermions, the action of $P$ is deduced from character formulas of $so(2n+2)$. For a set of $n$ parabosons, the known spectrum of $P$ yields new character formulas of particular $osp(2|2n)$ representations.

candidates.title: Optimal homological stability: bounding secondary terms of Cohen-Lenstra moments and $S_d$-fields over $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$
candidates.abstract: We prove an explicit stability line for the homology $H_i(\mathrm{Hur}_n^c,\mathbb{Q})$ of any Hurwitz space associated to a finite rack $c$ depending only on its homology up to some finite $n$. Moreover, as the range of $n$ increases, the slope of the resulting stability line converges to the optimal slope. Thus, for any Hurwitz space, a finite computation will yield near-optimal bounds on secondary terms for the corresponding arithmetic statistics problem. Our theorem also applies more generally to higher order stability, Frobenius weights, and braided vector spaces. As a special case of our theorem, we can deduce stability lines depending only on when $H_0(\mathrm{Hur}^c_n,\mathbb{Q})$ stabilizes, which are sharp in some cases. We apply this to two families of Hurwitz spaces to obtain bounds on the secondary term for (1) the number of $S_d$-degree $d$ function fields with squarefree discriminant, and (2) Cohen-Lenstra moments.

candidates.title: A Free Lunch: Gradient Averaging Achieves Optimal Statistical Efficiency in Newton Sketch
candidates.abstract: We study statistical inference for online sketched Newton methods, in which each Newton system is approximately solved by an inner randomized sketching solver. Existing work reveals a computational--statistical trade-off: the sketching solver (and its accelerated variants) reduces the per-step cost of Newton methods from $O(d^3)$ to $O(d^2)$, but the randomness introduced by sketching also inflates the limiting covariance of both the last and the averaged Newton iterates. In this work, we address this trade-off via gradient averaging. We show that simply replacing the stochastic gradient with a moving average at each step can mitigate, and in some cases eliminate, the trade-off in Newton sketch. Importantly, gradient averaging requires no additional oracle evaluations and leaves the contraction bound of the inner sketching solver unchanged. In particular, we prove that the last sketched Newton iterate with gradient averaging attains a limiting covariance no larger than that without gradient averaging, while the averaged iterate even attains the minimax optimal limiting covariance, matching that of the exact Newton method. candidates.title: Extreme value statistics for majorisation partial orders
candidates.abstract: We study extreme-value phenomena for random samples in partially ordered sets through their meets and joins, the order-theoretic analogues of minima and maxima. In this paper we consider the probability simplex equipped with either UT-majorisation or majorisation, with samples drawn uniformly from the corresponding simplex. We analyse these extrema both at fixed dimension and as the dimension grows, identifying almost-sure collapse to the bottom or top elements and critical scalings with nondegenerate limiting laws.

candidates.title: Spectral Pricing of Corridor Products under Layered Local Volatility
candidates.abstract: We price corridor products under a $N$-layered local volatility, piecewise constant in the price and in time, with knock-out barriers. A spatial scale transformation and the GIT method reduce the killed Green's function to a symmetric tridiagonal system of fixed size $N-1$. With equal scaled layer widths the spectrum follows from one tridiagonal eigen-decomposition together with the explicit eigenfunctions that vanish at every interface. For general scaled layer widths an exact counting theorem locates every eigenvalue. Consecutive time intervals of constant volatility are connected by a matrix that re-expands the solution in the eigenbasis of the preceding interval, and the result converges exponentially in the number of retained terms in the eigenfunction expansion. Allowing the killing rate to vary between layers preserves this construction. On a single time interval, the corridor accrual distribution is then recovered by inverting the time and Fourier transforms, without introducing an additional state variable. Exact representations for Greeks and layer vegas follow by differentiation. In our benchmarks the method agrees with independent calculations near rounding error and ke

candidates.title: Stability of Parallel Transport Convolution under Riemannian Metric Perturbations
candidates.abstract: Geometric convolutions on Riemannian manifolds depend on the geometry of the underlying domain, making stability under metric perturbations a fundamental question in geometric deep learning. This paper studies this question for parallel transport convolution through methods from differential geometry and analysis. On a fixed compact manifold, we establish that, for a continuous input signal and a continuous reference kernel supported in a sufficiently small normal neighborhood, the convolution output depends continuously in $L^2$ on the Riemannian metric in the $C^2$-topology, under the specified localization and transport-path conventions. The analysis develops perturbation estimates for geodesics, parallel transport, Jacobi fields, and exponential maps, and uses these estimates to compare the transported kernels. A central difficulty is the cut locus, which obstructs uniform comparison of the transport construction over the entire manifold. We address this difficulty by combining uniform estimates away from the cut locus with integral bounds on neighborhoods of arbitrarily small volume, while also controlling the change in the Riemannian volume measure. The resulting qualitative

candidates.title: The Spectral Distribution of Matrix Least Squares Solutions, and the Ellipsoid Fitting Problem
candidates.abstract: We study the spectral distribution of the least squares solution to a random linear system whose unknown is a symmetric matrix. In the normalized and isotropic setting, we derive a closed-form description of the support of the spectral distribution. As an application, we consider the ellipsoid fitting problem: given $n$ standard Gaussian vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$, does there exist a centered ellipsoid passing through all of them? It was recently shown that this problem has a sharp phase transition at $n \approx d^2/4$. On the satisfiability side, unlike earlier results, these sharp results do not rely on least squares candidates. We show that the least squares candidates considered in earlier works have a threshold of positive semi-definiteness at $n \approx d^2/10$, which was previously observed numerically and predicted non-rigorously using statistical physics methods. Moreover, we show that the corresponding least squares dual certificates have a threshold of positive definiteness at $n \approx 2d^2/5$. Our approach combines several matrix concentration tools. A key technical ingredient, which may be of independent interest, is showing that a certain kernel matrix is well-condit

candidates.title: The Holomorphic-Topological Poisson Sigma Model and Quantization of Affine W-algebras
candidates.abstract: We construct explicit deformation quantizations of classical principal affine $W$-algebras for every simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ using the holomorphic-topological Poisson sigma model of A. Khan and K. Zeng. A linear differential-graded presentation identifies the universal bulk with Chern--Simons theory near a principal nilpotent background, where holomorphic gauge gives a finite, 1-loop exact quantization. The quantum oper boundary observables form the principal affine $W$-algebra at level $k-h^\vee\hbar$; we also obtain this level shift directly for affine current algebras. For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we prove a perturbative quantum equivalence between Chern--Simons theory and three-dimensional chiral gravity, including their oper and Dirichlet boundary conditions, and determine the quantum relation between their parameters.

candidates.title: Unique continuation for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
candidates.abstract: We prove a unique continuation property for eigenstates of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian, viewed as functions of the electron configuration with values in the spin-photon space. The vector potential may lie in $L^6_\mathrm{loc}$, with its divergence, curl, and the scalar potential in $L^p_\mathrm{loc}$ for some $p>2$. As an application, we prove a Hohenberg-Kohn theorem at positive coupling strength: the spin-summed ground-state density and combined current density determine the external potentials up to a gauge transformation and an additive constant.

candidates.title: Sobolev theory for the inverse problem of time-dependent density functional theory on the torus
candidates.abstract: We show that, given a sufficiently regular time-dependent density, there exists a unique potential such that the Schrödinger equation with this external potential has the prescribed one-particle density. We treat densities that are twice differentiable in time and of finite Sobolev regularity in space; the resulting potentials are continuous in time and of finite Sobolev regularity in space. Our method of proof is to rewrite the problem as a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a loss of derivatives, which we in turn handle with a completion-of-the-square argument. This is a refinement of our recent work [Lauritsen, Lewin, and Oldenburg, arXiv:2609.08984], which handled this loss of derivatives using the Cauchy-Kovalevskaya theorem and treated analytic-in-space densities and potentials.

candidates.title: $H_2$-optimal riblet profiles for turbulence suppression in channel flows
candidates.abstract: The drag-reducing properties of streamwise-elongated surface corrugations, commonly referred to as riblets, have been extensively studied through experiments, simulations, and reduced-order modeling. Notably, the linearized Navier-Stokes framework introduced by Ran, Zare, and Jovanovic (J. Fluid Mech., vol. 906, 2021) employs volume penalization to model riblet-induced boundary conditions and predict drag reduction. These approaches typically quantify drag reduction as a function of a single geometric parameter, such as spanwise spacing or groove cross-sectional area, evaluated over fixed riblet shapes. As a result, identifying optimal riblet geometries across a broader design space often necessitates exhaustive parametric studies. To address this problem, we propose an optimization framework for the systematic design of optimal riblet shapes. Accordingly, we reformulate the volume penalization term in the linearized dynamics as a structured state-feedback operator. Targeting maximal suppression of turbulence, we pose a composite optimization problem that minimizes the steady-state variance of velocity fluctuations and riblet-induced dynamical augmentations while maintaining a cons

candidates.title: Large Language Models as Nonlinear Dynamical Systems: The Three Clocks of Depth, Training, and Generation
candidates.abstract: Language models are dynamical systems. A transformer is iterated over its layers, over the steps of its training and over the tokens it generates, and on each of these three clocks it shows behavior that nonlinear dynamics has studied for a century: fixed points, bifurcations, synchronization, chaos and noise-driven escape from potential wells. The two communities rarely meet, so this behavior is often rediscovered under new names. We build a bridge between them. To describe, we condense about 200 papers into the Three-Clock Dictionary, which maps fifteen concepts of nonlinear dynamics onto each clock and marks every correspondence as proved, measured or conjectured, and we show each concept in a mechanical system and in a language model side by side. To explain, we derive reduced-order models: the softmax is a Boltzmann distribution, gradient descent an Euler step on a nonlinear spring, a loss spike a ball thrown out of a stiff valley, attention on the circle a Kuramoto model, and a repetition loop a well that deepens while it is occupied. We then test these explanations on open language models, on a laptop CPU. Escape from repetition loops in GPT-2 and Pythia follows the Arrheniu

candidates.title: Axioms for relative entropy
candidates.abstract: For normal states of arbitrary von Neumann algebras, we characterize positive finite multiples of Araki relative entropy among non-degenerate divergences. The axioms are monotonicity under normal unital completely positive maps, tensor additivity, superadditivity for product second states, and separate lower semicontinuity in the predual norm. Alternatively, a conditional-expectation identity replaces the two tensor assumptions. The proof uses order bounds and asymptotic estimates on tensor powers. An appendix proves the known analytic estimates needed here, using standard modular theory and Haagerup L^p spaces. We also obtain the corresponding characterization in the C* algebraic setting.

candidates.title: Mean curvature flow into an ambient Riemannian manifold evolving by Ricci-Bourguignon flow
candidates.abstract: We study the mean curvature flow in Riemannian manifolds evolving by the Ricci-Bourguignon flow. Using DeTurck's trick, we establish short-time existence and uniqueness for the mean curvature flow in this time-dependent ambient geometry. In the case where the ambient metric evolves by a self-similar solution to the Ricci-Bourguignon flow, we characterize the associated mean curvature solitons and derive a Huisken monotonicity-type formula adapted to the Ricci-Bourguignon setting. As a consequence, we show that, in compact ambient manifolds, type-I singularities of the mean curvature flow in a gradient shrinking Ricci-Bourguignon soliton background have, after suitable parabolic rescaling, weighted minimal hypersurfaces as their limiting models, while in the noncompact setting, we establish the corresponding result for a gradient shrinking Schouten soliton background. This provides a geometric framework for understanding how the ambient scalar curvature influences the formation and structure of singularity models for the mean curvature flow. We also show how to construct explicit examples of mean curvature flow in a gradient Ricci-Bourguignon soliton background.

candidates.title: Almost Controlled: The FDR of Benjamini-Hochberg on Weighted Conformal p-Values
candidates.comment: 55 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Main text 10 pages; full proofs in the appendices
candidates.abstract: Weighted conformal p-values generalize conformal inference to cases with covariate shift. One way to use them is to pass them to the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure, either to decide which test units to select or to detect outliers. But weighted conformal p-values may not be positively dependent, so we want to know: does BH still control the false discovery rate (FDR) in finite samples? Based on experiments, it appears to, but we prove it doesn't. We give two counterexamples, certified in exact rational arithmetic, where the FDR exceeds its target level $q$. We also identify how large the difference between the FDR and $q$ can be. With $n$ calibration points, $m$ test units and weight ratio $B$, the relative excess $\mathrm{FDR}/q-1$ is bounded by a function of $n$, $m$, $B$ and $q$ that is of order $\sqrt{Bm/(nq)}$ when $Bm/(nq)$ is small. The bound holds for every configuration with $B\le n$ and every $n$. This order can be reached when multiple non-null test units share a common threshold: in a Poisson-limit model, that configuration's excess is $c(q)\sqrt{Bm/(nq)}$ to first order as $B/n\to0$ and then $m\to\infty$. candidates.title: Ice and mirrors
candidates.abstract: Given a mirror pair of smooth affine principal upper cluster varieties admitting reddening sequences, we show that homological mirror symmetry for principal cluster varieties -- assumed compatible with certain cluster structures -- descends under freezing. This allows us to induct on the following class. A skew-symmetrizable matrix is peelable if, by mutations and removing sinks or sources, it can be reduced to the empty matrix; it is sub-peelable if it is a principal submatrix of a peelable matrix. We establish homological mirror symmetry for full rank upper cluster varieties whose mutable matrix is sub-peelable. We show sub-peelability for the Fock--Goncharov SL(n) quiver for any compact surface with nonempty boundary, all of whose boundaries have markings. Consequently, we establish homological mirror symmetry between the moduli of decorated SL(n) local systems and the corresponding pinned PGL(n) spaces. The results were obtained using ChatGPT Astra.

candidates.title: Toeplitz coefficients and the Lu-Tian correspondence on Sasakian manifolds
candidates.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact embeddable strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold with Reeb field $T$ and Szeg\H o projection $Π$. Herrmann, Hsiao, Marinescu and the second author showed, for any volume form, that the semi-classical cut-offs $χ(k^{-1}ΠPΠ)$ of first-order elliptic self-adjoint Toeplitz operators have full asymptotic expansions. For $P=-\sqrt{-1}T$ and $T$-invariant volume forms, Chang, Herrmann and Hsiao showed that the diagonal coefficients are $a_{j}\intχ(t)t^{n-j}dt$ with local invariants $a_{j}$, computed $a_{0}$ and $a_{1}$, and used normal forms in the Sasakian case. We add one step: on a compact Sasakian manifold, regular or not, $a_{j}=a_{j}(g^{T})/(2π^{n+1})$, where $a_{j}(\cdot)$ is the universal Bergman kernel polynomial and $g^{T}$ the transverse Kähler metric; no line bundle on $X$ is needed. This gives an exact correspondence: the logarithmic term of the Szeg\H o kernel vanishes to infinite order over an open set if and only if $a_{j}(g^{T})=0$ there for all $j\ge n+1$, which for circle bundles is a local form of the theorem of Lu and Tian with its converse. candidates.title: Non-factorisable Yangian Lax matrices through oscillators
candidates.abstract: We construct oscillator realisations of Yangian Lax operators in type $A$, with particular interest in non-factorisable operators associated with prime snake modules. Our construction applies to finite-dimensional skew representations of $Y(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$. We prove that these representations are generated by the tensor vacuum in suitably ordered tensor products of oscillator representations. Their Lax operators are obtained by restricting the corresponding products of linear oscillator Lax operators to these submodules. We determine the vacuum eigenvalues and Drinfeld polynomials, and give a determinant formula for the dimensions directly in terms of the highest loop weights. A $21$-dimensional example illustrates the construction, including an explicit basis and a transfer-matrix identity.

candidates.title: High-probability Uniform Mixing via Dobrushin Contraction and Accelerated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
candidates.abstract: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, since its invention and subsequent rise to widespread use, has been motivated by its ability to accelerate convergence to equilibrium compared to diffusive methods, both in terms of dependence on condition number and dimension. In the present work, we establish this acceleration simultaneously in both aspects for critically damped Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin with persistent uniforms. More precisely, for target measures $μ(dx)\propto e^{-U(x)}dx$ with $m$-strongly convex, $L$-gradient Lipschitz, and $L_H$-Frobenius Hessian Lipschitz potentials, we show that the method mixes to $\varepsilon$-accuracy in total variation using $\mathcal O\bigl((κ^{1/2}+L_H^{1/2}m^{-3/4})\,d^{1/4}\bigr)$ gradient evaluations up to logarithmic factors, both uniformly over starting points in domains of high equilibrium probability and from warm starts. The proof incorporates ideas from previous studies by Bou-Rabee and Chen et al. that show either aspect of acceleration separately, into novel coupling technology. This new coupling technology for general Markov chains extends earlier frameworks aimed at capturing fast local equilibration in the presence of slow global mixi

candidates.title: Odd faces as a parameter for maximum independent set in embedded graphs
candidates.abstract: We give a polynomial-time algorithm for finding a maximum weight independent set in a graph embedded in a surface of bounded genus and with a bounded number of vertex-disjoint odd faces. In particular, we obtain an algorithm for graphs with an even-faced embedding in a torus and for planar graphs with a bounded number of odd faces, answering a question of Thomassé (2018) and a question of Choi, Gorsky, Kim, McFarland, and Wiederrecht (2025) respectively. We reduce the original problem to finding a minimum cost non-negative integer circulation with homology constraints in the dual of a certain double cover of the original graph.

candidates.title: The system of length sets of transfer Krull monoids over $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$
candidates.abstract: Let $H$ be a Krull monoid with class group $G$ and suppose that each class contains a prime divisor. There are precisely nine groups (up to isomorphism) for which the set of distances of $H$ is contained in $\{1, 2\}$. For all these groups, except for $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$, the system of length sets has been written down explicitly. In this paper we close this gap and determine the system of length sets when the class group is isomorphic to $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$.

candidates.title: Cyclic homology of Sheaf Categories
candidates.abstract: In this note, we explain the circle action on the Hochschild homology of categories of sheaves and their admissible subcategories in terms of the six-functor formalism using factorization homology, including (quasi-)coherent sheaves on derived stacks, sheaves on manifolds with prescribed microsupports, and Tamarkin categories with prescribed microsupports. We also explain the Gysin sequence for $C_\ell$ and $S^1$-(co)invariants and the Künneth sequence for $S^1$-(co)invariants of the Hochschild homology relative to any complex-oriented symmetric monoidal category.

candidates.title: Polynomial twisted periods and affine vertex algebras
candidates.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Kang, Lawrie, and Song that Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of a simply-laced boundary admissible affine vertex algebra is isomorphic to the Jacobian ring of an invariant potential obtained by lifting a polynomial twisted period from a Cartan subalgebra via the Chevalley isomorphism. We further identify the $C_2$-algebras of the corresponding Drinfeld-Sokolov reductions with the Jacobian rings of the restrictions of this potential to Slodowy slices. We also extend the Jacobian presentation to non-simply-laced principal boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, where the restriction of the potential to the Cartan subalgebra satisfies a Dunkl-singularity equation with root-length-dependent multiplicities.

candidates.title: Postselection on Halting and Reductions to the Halting Problem
candidates.abstract: A probabilistic Turing machine is an ordinary Turing machine that may also toss fair coins, with no limit on its running time or memory. If it always halts, it decides only computable problems. Aaronson et al. studied machines that may run forever on some coin tosses, with the answer read only from the runs that halt. Suppose the correct answer must be more than twice as likely as the wrong one. They showed that these machines decide exactly the problems solvable with a fixed list of questions about the halting problem. They asked what happens when the correct answer need only be the more likely one. We show that the machines then decide exactly the problems solvable by asking such questions one after another, each chosen after the earlier answers. We also show that the factor two can be replaced by any fixed factor greater than one. A machine may promise two numbers: a lower bound on its probability of halting, and a lower bound on its probability of being right when it halts. From these two numbers we compute exactly how many questions fixed in advance the machine can replace. The main idea is that probability acts as a budget for how often a computable guess may change its mind.

candidates.title: Spectral Landmarks: Alignment of Landmark Kernel Translates with the Leading Eigenfunctions of a Kernel Operator
candidates.abstract: We study the problem of choosing $m$ landmark points so that the span of the kernel translates is as close as possible to the leading $s$-dimensional eigenspace of a positive-definite kernel. The natural measure is the Hilbert-Schmidt operator discrepancy between the reproducing-kernel-Hilbert-space (RKHS) projectors onto the two subspaces. We give a closed form spectral alignment function in terms of the truncated Mercer kernel and relate it to the classical integrated power function (Nyström trace error) through a two-sided sandwich bound. Minimizing the function by gradient descent on the landmark coordinates produces landmark sets that are evenly spaced. Theoretical results show that optimal configurations are those whose eigenfunction sampling matrix is a scaled isometry. On homogeneous spaces these are exactly the minimal equal-weight cubature rules for products of leading eigenfunctions, and for every $m\ge s$ they are the configurations whose sampled eigenfunctions form a unit-norm tight frame. candidates.title: Ternary-Valued FDTD Method for Nonlinear Optics: Third-Harmonic Generation on a Multiplier-Free Solver
candidates.abstract: I show that a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) solver with field variables restricted to the ternary alphabet $\{-1,0,+1\}$ can reproduce nonlinear optical physics quantitatively on both CPUs and field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). Building on the general ternary-valued FDTD algorithm, in which each Yee cell stores an integer state that accumulates the discrete curl of neighbouring symbols without being drained, I extend the scheme to inhomogeneous and Kerr media and to Mur absorbing boundaries, without performing any multiplication operations. Dielectric contrast is implemented as a multiplexer, since the difference between ternary symbols takes only a few values, the instantaneous Kerr nonlinearity as a coefficient look-up table and the Mur boundary coefficients as canonical signed-digit shift--add chains. The scheme reproduces the third-harmonic conversion efficiency of a floating-point reference to within $1.4\%$. A symmetry of the governing physics, expressed through the even harmonics forbidden by centrosymmetric $χ^{(3)}$, provides a reference-free self-check for both ternary and floating-point models. candidates.title: Radar Waveform Design via Convex Semidefinite Relaxation
candidates.abstract: The ambiguity function (AF) of a radar waveform describes its ability to resolve targets in range and Doppler. Designing a waveform that attains a prescribed AF magnitude is a phase retrieval problem with four trivial ambiguities, and a time- or band-limited pulse is determined up to these ambiguities by at most three times as many AF samples as it has time samples or frequencies. Existing solvers for the narrowband AF, however, are non-convex: they cannot guarantee that they reach the global minimizer, which is unique only up to the trivial ambiguities, so the recovered pulse depends on the starting point. This letter addresses this gap by lifting the problem to positive semidefinite matrices supported on the pulse band, where each AF sample becomes the magnitude of a linear functional. In the lifted space, recovery is formulated as a convex program, and a dual certificate provides a sufficient condition for exactness. The proposed algorithm, wavex, combines an initialization by relaxed reflections, convex semidefinite surrogate steps, and a local polish. Numerical experiments show that wavex accurately recovers band-limited pulses from complete AFs and from AFs with most of their

candidates.title: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
candidates.abstract: We exhibit a complex Hadamard matrix of nonzero defect which is isolated among complex Hadamard matrices, up to Hadamard equivalence. This counterexample is realized by a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of size $13$, with entries roots of order $6$ of unity. In the language of commuting squares, this shows that the span condition, previously introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation, is not a necessary condition for isolation.

candidates.title: Character variety of the punctured sphere and the determinantal variety
candidates.abstract: We show that the SL(2;C) character variety of the n-punctured sphere is described via the determinantal variety defined by an n x n symmetric matrix of rank at most 4 whose entries are the traces of simple closed curves on the surface. This result generalizes the Fricke-Klein-Vogt relations to arbitrary n, and we determine the structure of the kernel of the associated matrix.

candidates.title: Certified Algorithms for Gaussian Location Mixture NPMLEs via Discretized Gradient Flows
candidates.abstract: We study the computation of approximate nonparametric maximum likelihood estimators (NPMLEs) for Gaussian location mixtures in arbitrary dimension $d\ge 1$ via the Fisher-Rao gradient flow. We provide a certified algorithm based on an entropic proximal discretization of the flow which, given a sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$, returns an absolutely continuous mixing measure $\tildeμ$ admitting an exact finite-dimensional representation and satisfying $\hat L_n-L_n(f_{\tildeμ})\le\varepsilon$. For almost every dataset $X_1,\cdots, X_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying $n>2(d+1)(m+1)^2$, where $m$ is the number of support points of the NPMLE, the algorithm requires $O(n\varepsilon^{-1}\log^{d+2}(1/\varepsilon))$ time. En route, we also establish results on the well-posedness and convergence properties of the continuous-time Fisher--Rao flow. In particular, initializing the flow at the uniform probability measure on a ball containing the convex hull of the observations, we show that $\hat L_n-L_n(f_{μ_t})=O(\log t/t)$. We also establish that, for almost every dataset satisfying the same condition on $n$ as above, the set of global maxima of the optimal score is the same as the support

candidates.title: Computing rare events in Lévy-driven systems via optimal control
candidates.abstract: We extend the optimal control formulation of sample path large deviation theory, which has proven effective for numerical computation of instantons and sharp probability estimates in stochastic differential equations with Gaussian noise, to systems with light-tailed Lévy noise. In the scaling limit of small jumps and high intensity, such systems satisfy a large deviation principle of Freidlin-Wentzell type, with a running cost given by the Legendre transform of the noise cumulant generating function. We propose to numerically minimize this cost over noise realizations subject to the system dynamics, which yields the instanton without having to solve Hamilton's equations, and naturally handles degenerate and multiplicative noise. When the cumulant generating function has a bounded domain, the cost grows only linearly for large noise, and instantons can contain jumps. We analyze when jumps are not only admissible but optimal, depending on the subleading behavior of the cost and on the drift, and show how jumps can be resolved numerically through a time reparameterization that freezes physical time. For continuous instantons, we derive Riccati and Fredholm determinant expressions for

candidates.title: Simulated Annealing with Topological Spatial Chunking for De Novo Protein Sequence Design
candidates.abstract: The inverse protein folding problem, designing a discrete amino acid sequence that spontaneously folds into a predefined macroscopic structure, remains a phenomenally demanding combinatorial challenge central to synthetic drug discovery. While algorithms like SA offer a baseline approach for navigating dense biomolecular energy landscapes, applying SA heuristics to large sequences is inherently frustrated by exponentially large search spaces and deep local energy minima. This study proposes a scalable sequence design architecture, Topological Spatial Chunking Simulated Annealing, based on a localized, exact-solving heuristic embedded within a global simulated-annealing wrapper. To fundamentally circumvent exponential scaling walls, we deploy a dynamic solver that segments the global molecular target into shallow, k-variable algorithmic windows. Crucially, rather than partitioning natively by sequential 1D chronology, we introduce topological spatial chunking, which dynamically groups discrete variables based on Euclidean spatial proximity to preserve critical non-local thermodynamic correlations. The spatially localized sub-problems are solved deterministically via exact enumeratio

candidates.title: Log-optimal two-sample testing by betting
candidates.abstract: For each standard Borel observation space, we construct a single anytime-valid two-sample procedure that is asymptotically log-optimal for every pair of unknown probability laws and every limiting ratio of diverging sample sizes, including zero and infinity. For independent balanced pairs, the optimal log-wealth rate is $2\JS(P,Q)$, where $\JS$ is the Jensen--Shannon divergence. Unequal sizes yield weighted Jensen--Shannon information and the one-sample limit $\log W(n_1,n_2)/n_2\to\KL(Q\|P)$ when $n_1/n_2\to\infty$. Refining finite partitions and logarithmic-loss learning with measurable characteristic kernels provide universal constructions. Our main contribution is the generality of our construction, and its connections to classical batch efficiency notions. Practical implementations allow continuous classifier fine-tuning, as demonstrated on finite alphabets, Gaussian data, and handwritten digits.

candidates.title: High-dimensional limit theorems for adaptive variants of SGD I: Ballistic limits
candidates.abstract: We develop the high-dimensional effective dynamics for adaptive, momentum-based variants of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD). These effective dynamics are given by a Markov process. They key observation is that the non-Markovianity in the algorithm due to the exponential moving average and preconditioning can be treated using the method of averaging. Our approach applies to a broad class of algorithms including to Adaptive momentum estimation (ADAM), Momentum orthogonalized by Newton-Schultz (MUON), and its variants. It also applies to a broad class of learning tasks, such at tensor PCA, Gaussian projective models, teacher-student networks, and a multi-layer neural network trained on the XOR problem using a hybrid of MUON and ADAM as commonly done in practice. We demonstrate how to this technique can give precise, quantitative comparisons between algorithms. In particular, we find interesting phenomena, such as the cross-over phenomenon where online SGD has better generalization than ADAM early in training until the learning curves cross and ADAM dominates. Furthermore, we prove a version of the Edge of Stability phenomenon. In particular, we introduce an analogue of the infinity

candidates.title: Asymptotic stability of axisymmetric perturbations of near-horizon extremal Kerr with a Schwarzian-deformed throat
candidates.abstract: We study the asymptotic stability of axisymmetric gravitational perturbations of the near-horizon geometries of (near-)extremal Kerr black holes and consider the family of backgrounds in which the AdS$_{2}$ factor of NHEK is deformed by a Schwarzian mode. Requiring the Killing parameter to be local in the background makes the Gelfand--Dikii polynomials natural solutions of the Killing equation, and that locality requirement brings stationary solutions of the Korteweg-de Vries equation. candidates.abstract: We investigate when the braided monoidal $\infty$-categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators of $3$-dimensional topological quantum field theories are invertible in the higher Morita category, so that they determine invertible $4$-dimensional anomaly theories. candidates.title: No free lattice contains an infinite ascending chain of copies of FL(3)
candidates.comment: 59 pages, 13 figures; the main theorem is checked in Agda; the formal development is available at https://github.com/ualib/agda-deans-problem
candidates.abstract: No free lattice contains an infinite strictly ascending chain of sublattices isomorphic to FL(3), the free lattice on three generators; this answers a question that R. A. Dean asked and the second author's 1997 notes on the problem left open. Every such chain would yield, inside FL(3), a coherent chain of proper self-embeddings $Θ_0, Θ_1, Θ_2, \dots$ with $Θ_k \circ Θ_j = Θ_j$ for $j < k$, so that each later embedding fixes the image of each earlier one pointwise. Every proper self-embedding of FL(3) whose fixed sublattice contains a free generating triple fixes one of the three generators, say $z$, because a power of it or of its dual lies above the identity, and a self-embedding that moves every generator and lies above the identity fixes at most eleven elements. Up to duality, a proper self-embedding fixing the image of such a $Θ_1$ pointwise fixes only elements above $z \wedge (x \vee y)$, where no free generating triple containing $z$ can lie. We also verify the one-step example of the 1997 notes, prove that no step toward such a chain is self-similar, and show that the configuration the argument rules out at length three does occur at length two. candidates.title: Invariant measures with uniform projection on surfaces and billiards
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we study probability measures on the unit tangent bundle which are invariant under the geodesic flow and whose projection to the base manifold is the normalized Riemannian volume. We show that the Liouville measure is the only such measure on a complete oriented surface of finite area with ergodic geodesic flow. In particular, this resolves a conjecture of Katok--Knieper--Weiss in dimension two. The same holds for ergodic planar billiards with piecewise C2 boundary, such as the Bunimovich stadium, the Sinai billiard, and generic polygons. The proof combines the Fourier analysis in the fibers with holomorphic functions on the transport twistor space. As a consequence, on these surfaces and on the Bunimovich stadium, a high-energy sequence of normalized Laplacian eigenfunctions tends to be equidistributed in the phase space if and only if it tends to be equidistributed in the physical space. In particular, on every stadium, every failure of equidistribution in the phase space implies scarring in the physical space.
